title: SRE weekly ops sync — notes & reliability review (2026-03-08)
body:
Prep for weekly ops sync (2026-03-08) — quick notes / agenda / follow-ups

Attendees: Alex, Priya, Marcus, Sofia, Jordan (+ optional: oncall rotation)
Timebox: 45m

Agenda:
- Quick wins / shoutouts (2-3m)
- SLO check + error budget status (10m)
- Paging trends & noise analysis (10m)
- Top incidents since last sync (10m)
- Action items & owners (8-10m)

SLOs snapshot (for review) — pull numbers from reliability dashboard before meeting:
- Hosted API availability SLO: 99.95% (monthly)
  - Current monthly: 99.917% (burning) — ~0.033% over threshold -> ~2.3h outage-equivalent burned this month
  - Recent contributors: incident INC-2026-02-db-restarts (~45m) + embedding model high-latency tail (~30m cumulative)
- Embeddings latency SLO (p99 <= 800ms): currently p99 = 920ms (rolling 7d) — risk of breach if trend continues
- Dedicated tenant control-plane SLO: 99.9% — current 99.96% (OK)

Quick notes on error budgets:
- Hosted API error budget is low — recommend pause risky infra changes for next 72h or gate with canary and rapid rollback plan
- Coordinate with release-engineering to freeze non-critical deploys to model-serving stack until burn stabilizes

Paging trends (last 7 days):
- Total pages: 18 (down from 24 prior week) — good trend overall but still noise-heavy
- Top alert sources:
  1) Redis CPU spikes on rds-shared-1 (7 pages) — correlated with bursty indexing jobs from solutions-eng test namespace
  2) KV cache eviction alerts (4 pages) — increased cache miss rate after recent quantized model rollout (see PR #4723)
  3) API gateway 5xx spikes during eu-west-1 rolling deploy (3 pages) — autoscaling delayed due to scheduling constraints
- Pager fatigue notes: most duplicate pages are from redis CPU alert flapping — need better dedupe + runbook review

Top incidents (since last sync):
- INC-2026-02-db-restarts — severity 2
  - Summary: a sequence of DB restarts on primary due to kernel OOM triggered by a noisy background compaction job on dedicated telemetry DB
  - Impact: brief metadata write errors, some failed writes surfaced as 500s to hosted API (45m window)
  - Root cause: compaction job memory use spike + insufficient oom scoring on telemetry container
  - Mitigation: throttled compaction, bumped memory request on telemetry job, added oom-killer affinity rules
  - Follow-ups: add memory safety checks to compaction job (Sofia), add runbook step to failover quicker (Marcus)

- Embeddings p99 latency regressions (linked JIRA) — ongoing
  - Summary: after quantized v2 rollout to GPU pool B, p99 for embeddings increased ~15% for long sequences
  - Hypothesis: kernel selection path chooses slower fallback for some sequence lengths after quantization; KV cache hit patterns changed
  - Mitigations in flight: revert quantized v2 for small subset of traffic (canary), enable extra batching for long-seq requests
  - Owner: Priya leading investigation with applied-ml + serving-runtime

- api-gw 5xx spikes during eu-west rolling deploy
  - Summary: during svc rollout autoscaler didn't scale fast enough -> queue pressure -> transient 502/503
  - Mitigation: reverted rollout, increased horizontal pod autoscaler buffer for gateway
  - Action: add deploy-time autoscale pre-flight checks to release engineering checklist (Jordan)

Action items (owner / due):
- Sofia: add memory safety and OOM detection to telemetry compaction job; add automated alert if compaction mem > 70% of requested (due 2026-03-12)
- Marcus: update failover runbook for primary DB with faster detection and failover window guidance; test failover in staging (due 2026-03-11)
- Priya: continue embeddings p99 investigation, run kernel selection profiling and coordinate with serving-runtime; report back w/ root cause hypotheses (due 2026-03-10)
- Jordan: add autoscaler pre-flight checks to release checklist + rollout playbook (due 2026-03-14)
- Alex (me): temporarily pause non-essential infra/model deploys that touch hosted-api SLO until error budget improves; notify release-engineering and product (done: slack note posted) (review 2026-03-10)
- Team: consolidate duplicate pager rules for redis CPU alerts; implement dedupe window (proposal by Marcus) (due 2026-03-15)

Notes / talking points for meeting:
- Emphasize we have low but still recoverable error budget — prefer safety first for next 72h
- Ask Priya for quick status on embeddings canary (are we seeing improvement after partial revert?)
- Confirm Sofia timeline for compaction changes and whether staging test plan is adequate
- Decide whether to temporarily increase SLO alert thresholds (only if we can provide mitigations & timeline) — prefer not to unless required

Follow-ups after meeting (to capture):
- Capture action items in JIRA (I'll create JIRA tickets for each owner and link back to this doc)
- Update reliability dashboard notes with incident summaries + postmortem links once available
- Schedule a shorter follow-up check-in (15m) mid-week if embeddings p99 not improving

Notes-to-self / scratchpad (things to check before meeting):
- Pull exact SLO numbers from reliability dashboard + last 30d burn chart
- Verify affected tenants list for INC-2026-02 to include customer-facing impact (if any)
- Confirm canary traffic split and whether rollback completed successfully for quantized v2
- Prepare a 2-slide summary for execs if asked (1) SLO health + biggest risk, (2) immediate mitigations + blockers

Misc / FYI:
- Related PR: github:pull/4723 (quantized v2 rollout) — keep thumb on CI and perf tests
- Confluence: reliability-dashboard has updated embedding latency charts (link above)

End of notes. Will tidy post-meeting with decisions + JIRA links.
